title: Verify Claude Code cwd metadata comes from JSONL body
body:
## Background

#102 tracks local multi-agent observability as radar. One comment raised a source-specific correctness risk that is narrow enough to route without turning agenttrace into a live dashboard: Claude Code stores session files under `~/.claude/projects/<encoded-cwd>/<uuid>.jsonl`, but that encoded directory name is not a reversible project path. Any parser/report metadata that needs a project cwd should prefer the authoritative `cwd` value from JSONL records when present.

## Evidence

- #102 comment describes the concrete failure mode: Claude Code project-directory encoding can collapse `/`, `\`, and `:` into similar path fragments, so deriving a project name or cwd from the directory can mislabel sessions.
- Product read-only check of `origin/master` at `6fb3917` found Claude JSONL parsing in `internal/engine/engine.go` and session loading via `LoadSession(path)`.
- Current `Session` has `Name` and `Path`; `parseClaudeCodeJSONL(raw)` does not expose a structured cwd/project metadata field from JSONL body records.
- The check did not find evidence that agenttrace currently reverse-decodes `~/.claude/projects/<encoded-cwd>` into a cwd, so this is a focused correctness/metadata check rather than a confirmed misparse bug.

## User value

Users comparing Claude Code sessions across repositories need project/session metadata that does not silently derive from an irreversible encoded path. Correct cwd provenance improves report trust when sessions are grouped, exported, or compared downstream.

## Adoption rationale

This keeps Developer experience and Reliability value aligned with local multi-source observability while staying inside agenttrace's completed-session evidence model.

## Suggested scope

- Add or verify a minimal Claude Code JSONL fixture where a record includes an authoritative `cwd` field.
- Ensure parser/session/report metadata uses the JSONL body `cwd` when a cwd/project field is exposed.
- Ensure no code path attempts to reconstruct cwd by replacing characters in `~/.claude/projects/<encoded-cwd>`.
- If agenttrace chooses not to expose cwd metadata yet, add a regression guard or documented parser note proving the encoded directory is not treated as authoritative cwd.

## Non-goals

- Do not build a live multi-agent monitor, watcher, or orchestration UI.
- Do not index prompt content by default.
- Do not infer project paths from private logs beyond local fixture-backed metadata.
- Do not claim Antigravity, Qwen export, or other new source support.

## Acceptance criteria

- A test fixture covers a Claude Code JSONL session whose file path has an encoded project directory and whose JSONL record has an explicit `cwd`.
- The test proves any exposed cwd/project metadata comes from the JSONL body, not from encoded path reversal.
- If cwd is not currently exposed, the test or parser note proves encoded path reversal is absent and future exposure must use body metadata.
- Existing `go test ./...` and relevant CI checks pass.
- Public docs, if touched, use conservative wording and avoid live-dashboard or hosted-observability claims.

## Suggested lane

lane/parser, priority/P2, status/ready-for-agent

## Risk

Medium. The implementation surface is small, but incorrect project metadata can mislead downstream reports and future multi-agent comparison features.

## Source

source/product: Product follow-up from #102, with read-only code inspection on `origin/master` at `6fb3917`.

title: [Product] Surface local cost-driver notes for token/context waste
body:
## Background

agenttrace already reports local tokens, estimated cost, context pressure, large parameters, retry loops, repeated tool output, and slow-run evidence. A small product gap remains: users can see that a session was expensive, but the report does not always connect that cost to an avoidable local evidence pattern in plain language.

## Evidence

- Product validation on `origin/master` at `08cf27e` generated demo overview JSON with `total_tokens`, `total_cost`, `health_trend`, `tool_fail_rate`, and incident timeline evidence, but no explicit local "possible cost driver" explanation in `summary`.
- Current docs already position slow-task diagnosis around large params and context pressure, so this is an explanation-layer refinement rather than a new capability claim.
- Public ecosystem signal shows developers are actively trying to understand and reduce token/context waste in Claude Code and Codex-style workflows:
  - https://claudecodeguides.com/why-claude-prompts-use-too-many-tokens/
  - https://docs.bswen.com/blog/2026-04-28-codex-token-optimization/
  - https://token-saver.ai/
  - https://claudskills.com/skills/fleet-auditor/
- Duplicate check found no existing issue for `context pressure token waste cost`, `large params context pressure cost driver diagnostics`, or `token waste avoidable spend context`.

## User value

When a local session has high spend or token usage, users should quickly understand whether the likely driver was context pressure, large tool parameters/output, retry loops, or long idle/rework patterns, without reading every raw trace.

## Adoption rationale

Developer experience improves when the overview report turns existing local evidence into a conservative next diagnostic clue. This strengthens Reliability value while staying local-first and privacy-preserving.

## Suggested scope

- Add a conservative `possible_cost_driver` or equivalent note to JSON overview summary or session-level output using existing evidence only.
- Surface the same idea in Markdown/HTML/text overview where appropriate, using wording such as "possible driver" rather than guaranteed savings.
- Prefer already-computed signals: context pressure, large parameters, repeated tool output/retry loop, high tool failure rate, long gaps, or high tokens per assistant turn if already available.
- Keep output deterministic and fixture-backed.

## Non-goals

- Do not index prompt content or raw conversation text.
- Do not add prompt compression, output suppression, memory capture, vector search, context injection, or MCP behavior.
- Do not build a billing dashboard, hosted telemetry, or external pricing integration.
- Do not claim guaranteed token savings.
- Do not add new parser/source support.

## Acceptance criteria

- Demo or fixture-backed overview output includes a conservative possible cost-driver note when existing local evidence supports one.
- JSON output remains stable and documented by the relevant report/output contract checks.
- Markdown/HTML/text output, if touched, uses local evidence wording and avoids hosted-observability or savings claims.
- `go test ./...` passes.
- Relevant CI scripts pass, especially report semantics, deterministic output, and output contract if changed.

## Suggested lane

lane/product, priority/P2, status/ready-for-agent

## Risk

Medium. The user-facing value is small but useful; the main risk is overclaiming causality from heuristic evidence, so wording must stay conservative.

## Source

source/product: Product validation and ecosystem signal scan on 2026-05-20.

## Summary

Major performance optimizations for agenttrace, focusing on session loading speed and TUI responsiveness.

## Key Improvements

### Session Cache (35x faster)
- ScanAllDirs() now uses session cache
- Non-TUI commands benefit from cache
- SQLite sessions cached with DB file mtime check

### Parallel Loading (4x faster cold start)
- LoadSessionsParallel() with worker pool pattern
- CPU-aware concurrency (max 8 workers)

### TUI Enhancements
- Mouse support (scroll, click)
- Session preview panel (wide terminals)
- Quick action menu (press x)
- Skeleton loading screen
- Vim navigation (ctrl+d/u, G)

### Benchmark Results

| Command | Before | After | Improvement |
|---------|--------|-------|-------------|
| --overview cold | 4.3s | 3.8s | 1.1x |
| --overview cached | 4.3s | 0.95s | 4.5x |
| --latest | 26s | 0.73s | 35x |

- internal/engine/fastjson.go - JSON parsing optimization
- internal/engine/memory.go - Memory pool utilities

title: Migrate AgentTrace to Rust v0.6.0
body:
## Summary

- migrate AgentTrace from the Go implementation to a Rust workspace with shared `agenttrace-core`, `agenttrace-tui`, and `agenttrace-cli` crates
- keep CLI and TUI in one `agenttrace` binary: no report flags opens the TUI, while automation/report flags run the CLI
- align CLI/TUI filtering, diagnostics, reports, search, waste analysis, doctor, pricing, history, and cache-backed session loading
- add session capability levels (`Detailed`, `Aggregate`, `Limited`), coverage reporting, background TUI refresh, and redacted Tool Steps
- expand parser coverage and deterministic generated fixtures, including SQLite-backed aggregate sources
- switch CI, release checks, installers, Homebrew formula, documentation, and public project surfaces to the Rust delivery path
- refresh the public showcase from a generated redacted 500-session snapshot

## Performance

Measured locally on Apple Silicon/macOS using release builds against the same 969 real session files (about 2.53 GiB). Explicit `-d` scans do not use SessionCache, so these numbers measure full discovery/parsing/report throughput rather than cache cold/warm startup.

| Workload | Go | Rust | Change |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| Overview | 16.76 s | 5.14 s | 3.26x faster |
| Latest | 16.21 s | 5.23 s | 3.10x faster |
| Search | 16.40 s | 5.39 s | 3.04x faster |
| Compare | 0.24 s | 0.07 s | 3.33x faster |
| Doctor | 0.53 s | 0.16 s | 3.25x faster |
| Process startup (`--version`) | 12.0 ms | 7.6 ms | 1.6x faster |
| Release binary | 12.0 MiB | 7.9 MiB | 35% smaller |

The initial Rust parser peaked around 1,041.5 MiB on the full corpus. Streaming JSONL objects instead of retaining a whole-file `Vec<serde_json::Value>` reduced peak RSS to 583.9 MiB (43.9% lower), slightly below the Go run at about 617 MiB. The same A/B run produced identical session count, total tokens, estimated cost, and total duration.

## User impact

- faster full-history analysis and lower CPU time
- cache-first TUI entry with background refresh when cached data exists
- one installable binary for interactive and automation workflows
- richer diagnostics and observability while avoiding storage of prompt, reply, tool-result, or tool-argument bodies in Tool Steps
- compatible generated testdata and Go-shaped cache/session contracts for migration safety

## Validation

- `cargo fmt --check`
- `cargo clippy --workspace -- -D warnings`
- `cargo test --workspace -- --test-threads=1` (109 tests)
- `cargo build --release -p agenttrace`
- `python3 scripts/generate-testdata.py --check`
- `python3 scripts/ci/check-single-binary-entrypoints.py`
- `scripts/ci/check-release-surfaces.sh`
- `scripts/ci/check-pages-artifact.sh site`
- real local CLI/TUI smoke checks and release-binary performance A/B

title: fix: harden untrusted-input handling and make reads truthful (cycles 1-4)
body:
## Summary

Three cycles of adversarial hardening plus a CI determinism fix, delivered as one commit (`93aaf053`, based on `e005952`):

- **Cycle 1 — parser arithmetic:** token and cost aggregation saturates instead of overflowing; negative usage clamps to zero; pricing is offline by default via a bundled dated snapshot; `pricing_source` labels no longer embed timestamps.
- **Cycle 2 — SQLite ingestion:** adversarial token columns saturate and negative values clamp on the `opencode.db`/`state.db` paths; sessions prefer stored session-row totals over derived aggregation with provenance disclosure (snapshot schema v5); unknown start times stay visible in an unknown-time bucket; the TUI exits with a clean error instead of panicking when stdout is not a terminal.
- **Cycle 3 — trustworthy strings:** UTF-16 escape repair reads escape hex from bytes, so a malformed `\u` escape followed by multi-byte UTF-8 no longer crashes every non-interactive action with exit 101 (adversarial unicode-escape corpus added); the fallback token estimate is CJK-aware and `reasoning_chars` counts characters, with new naming provenance; OpenCode `New session - <ts>` placeholder titles gate to message-derived names; `--version` wins over action validation; cache writes use per-writer unique temp files before the atomic rename.
- **Determinism:** `--demo --overview -f json` pins `scope.generated_at` to a fixed synthetic epoch so the deterministic-output check no longer flakes at second boundaries; real runs still stamp wall-clock time.

## Validation

- `cargo test --workspace`: **180/180** in debug **and** release (169 at campaign start)
- `cargo fmt --check` clean; `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets` 0 warnings
- All locally runnable CI steps of `.github/workflows/ci.yml` pass in CI order (the TUI real-smoke step is env-gated and needs `expect`, unavailable locally — skipped for the same reason CI skips it)
- Adversarial review: fuzzed unicode-escape alphabet (6 files × 500 seeded lines × 3 actions) — zero panics, zero exits outside {0,1,2}; verdict *pass_with_findings*, follow-ups recorded
- Full assessment/research/review records under `docs/reviews/`, `docs/research/`, `docs/stewardship/`; roadmap updated

## Notes for reviewers

Single squashed commit by design: cycles 1–3 share edited files, so only the combined state was validated end to end. The raw planning diff `docs/stewardship/2026-09-02-roadmap-cycle2-update.diff` was deliberately **not** committed (review P5-5: no raw diffs as documentation).

---

## Update — cycle 4 (`998ade8`, on top of `6632014` "ci: use self-hosted runner")

title: fix(parser): skip leading non-session lines in Oh My Pi JSONL
body:
## Problem

Every Oh My Pi session JSONL file fails to parse with `oh_my_pi: missing session header` (in my case: 203/203 files, so the whole provider effectively disappears from reports).

**Root cause:** Oh My Pi writes a `{"type":"title", ...}` line *before* the `{"type":"session", ...}` header in its session exports. The sniffing function `is_oh_my_pi_jsonl` already tolerates this — it scans all lines with `.any()` — but `parse_oh_my_pi_jsonl` requires the **first** JSONL object to be `type == "session"` and bails immediately otherwise. Sniffing accepts a file the parser then rejects, so the inconsistency only surfaces at parse time.

## Fix

Instead of bailing when the first object is not `type == "session"`, skip forward to the first session-header object (`continue`). Files that contain no session header at all still fail with the original `oh_my_pi: missing session header` error at the end of the loop, so no existing behavior is lost.

```diff
         if !seen_header {
-            if typ != "session" {
-                bail!("oh_my_pi: missing session header");
-            }
+            // Oh My Pi prepends non-session lines (e.g. {"type":"title",...})
+            // before the session header; skip anything until the first
+            // type == "session" object instead of bailing.
+            if typ != "session" {
+                continue;
+            }
```

## Verification

Local data set: 169 Oh My Pi session files (plus subagent artifacts).

- Before: `agenttrace --doctor` → Oh My Pi `found=203 parsed=0 failed=203`
- After: `agenttrace --doctor` → Oh My Pi `found=203 parsed=169 failed=34` (the remaining 34 are non-session subagent `.json` artifacts, not JSONL transcripts)
- Global overview goes from 323 → 492 sessions once omp sessions parse
- A previously failing file now reports correctly end-to-end (tokens, cost, health, anomalies)

Only `parse_oh_my_pi_jsonl` is touched; the trailing `if !seen_header { bail!() }` after the loop preserves the original error for header-less files.

title: build(windows): link the MSVC CRT statically
body:
The Windows release binaries are built for `*-pc-windows-msvc` with a dynamic CRT, so they import `VCRUNTIME140.dll` and the UCRT `api-ms-win-crt-*` DLLs. On a machine without the Visual C++ Redistributable they fail to start with `0xC0000135` (STATUS_DLL_NOT_FOUND); winget validation hit this on microsoft/winget-pkgs#430449.

This links the CRT statically for both Windows targets via `.cargo/config.toml`, so release binaries no longer need the redistributable. Non-Windows targets are unaffected.

Verification to do on the next release: the import table of the built `.exe` should no longer list `VCRUNTIME140.dll` or `api-ms-win-crt-*`.

title: fix(diagnostics): separate unmatched tool calls from explicit timeouts
body:
Reported in https://github.com/luoyuctl/agenttrace/discussions/2#discussioncomment-18737228.

## Problem
`tool_latencies` counted every tool call without a matching timestamped result as a **timeout**. That shape also comes from interrupted sessions, truncated exports, or results the parser could not pair. Downstream, `timeouts > 0` escalated the latency finding to `high`, produced a high-severity "Bound slow tool execution" recommendation, and showed `timeout` in the TUI.

## Change
- `ToolLatency.timeouts` now counts only results that are failures **and** explicitly mention a timeout (`timed out`, `timeout`, `deadline exceeded`).
- New `ToolLatency.unmatched` (`#[serde(default)]`) counts calls with no matching result; completion is unknown. It does not escalate severity.
- TUI shows `no result` vs `timeout`; detail line shows both counts.
- Session cache schema 19 → 20 so cached diagnostics are recomputed.

## Evidence (local history, 1,970 sessions)
- Before: 4,433 unmatched calls across 177 sessions were all reported as timeouts.
- After: 117 explicit timeouts across 53 sessions; the rest is reported as unmatched.

## Tests
- Call followed by end of input → `unmatched=1, timeouts=0`.
- Error results reporting `timed out` / `{"error":"deadline exceeded"}` → `timeouts=2`.
- Successful result mentioning "timeout" → not a timeout.
- `cargo clippy -D warnings`, workspace tests, and CI contract scripts pass locally.

<!-- This is an auto-generated comment: release notes by coderabbit.ai -->
## Summary by CodeRabbit

* **Diagnostics**
  * Tool latency reports distinguish explicit timeouts from calls with no matching result.
  * Summaries include unmatched-call counts and surface these calls even when measured latency is low. Matched calls are counted even when their duration falls outside the accepted range for latency statistics.
  * Timeout detection applies to failed results; successful results mentioning a timeout are not classified as timeouts.
* **Bug Fixes**
  * Slow-tool recommendations identify tools that exceed the latency threshold or report a timeout.
  * Previews show localized timeout or no-result annotations, prioritizing timeout when both conditions apply.
<!-- end of auto-generated comment: release notes by coderabbit.ai -->

title: feat(tui): adaptive 120 FPS motion and aligned layouts
body:
## Summary

Adds frame-paced motion to the explorer TUI and fixes the alignment problems found by rendering every screen (en/zh × 80x24, 120x30, 160x40, 220x50).

**Motion** (`crates/agenttrace-tui/src/motion.rs`, new)
- View slide + soft sweep on screen changes, overlay grow-in, selection wipe, notice type-in/out, count-up numbers in the header and preview, loading spinner + gauge shimmer, and a 14-day cost sparkline above the list.
- Effects only reuse the existing palette and are applied to the rendered buffer, so with motion off the frame is identical to before.
- Idle stays event-driven: nothing is drawn when nothing animates.

**Adaptive frame rate**
- A pacer measures each frame's render + terminal write time (writes block on a slow terminal, so backpressure shows up in the same number) and steps between 120 / 60 / 30 FPS: median of 8 frames, 1s cooldown to step down, 4s to step back up.
- Frames are scheduled from the previous deadline, so OS timer overshoot no longer caps 120 FPS near ~105; each frame is wrapped in synchronized output to avoid tearing.

**Performance**
- Explorer row order and header totals are memoized per filter generation. With ~2k real sessions a frame dropped from 8.7ms to 0.5ms, which was what kept the TUI from reaching 120 FPS.

**Layout fixes**
- Label/value blocks (context, cost, tools, storage, project, files) align on display width instead of hard-coded spaces, which broke in Chinese.
- File mtime shows local time instead of `SystemTime { tv_sec: … }`.
- Preview metric chips wrap as whole chips; footer hints drop whole entries instead of cutting mid-word; zero cost shows `$0`.
- Detail sidebar padding, no stray timeline rule, overlays sized to content, "no matches" in the command palette.

## Coordination

- Linked issue: none
- Protected public surface touched? no (TUI only; CLI/report output unchanged)
- Parser PR mergeability checked after latest `master`? n/a

## Validation

- [x] `cargo fmt --check`
- [x] `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings`
- [x] `cargo test -p agenttrace-core -p agenttrace-tui -p agenttrace` (182 passed; TUI 53, incl. 10 new motion/pacer tests)

title: feat(cli): --daily/--weekly/--monthly with --tz, and 5-hour --blocks
body:
#304 and #305 are merged; this branch is up to date with master.

Community pain points: 5-hour window / burn-rate tracking (ccusage#483, #146, CCUM#106) and timezone/day-boundary bugs (ccusage#778, codeburn#425, CCUM#121).

**Data**
- Each usage record keeps its timestamp (`Metrics.usage_points`), cached as compact `[ts, tokens, cost]` triples. Cache schema 22 → 23 (one-time rescan).
- Sessions without per-turn usage (text estimates, aggregate SQLite) fall back to one record at session start.

**CLI**
- `--daily` / `--weekly` (ISO, Monday) / `--monthly`: each record bucketed by its own time, so sessions crossing midnight are split.
- `--tz local|utc|+08:00` (default local; no new deps — fixed offsets only, IANA names rejected with a clear error).
- `--blocks`: 5-hour blocks (start at the hour of first activity; new block after 5h or a 5h gap) with tokens/min, $/hour, and end-of-block projection for the active block. `--token-limit` / `--cost-limit` add used/projected %.
- Output is labelled **estimated** (text note + `"estimated": true` in JSON) since provider limits are server-side.
- Text + JSON, en + zh-CN. Docs live in `docs/guides/usage-over-time.md`; READMEs only gain a link.

**Tests**: unit tests for tz parsing, midnight split, ISO weeks, months, block boundaries/projection, fallback; CLI integration test for tz bucketing, blocks JSON, bad tz, action conflicts.

title: workbuddy parser: unstated input_tokens basis + max(0) clamp turns a basis mismatch into silent zero
body: @/tmp/ghbody/issue-agenttrace.md

title: fix(parser): sum every WorkBuddy usage record instead of keeping the last
body:
Refs #310.

## Problem
`parse_workbuddy_jsonl` kept only the **last** usage record (`latest_usage`) and emitted it as a single meta event. WorkBuddy writes one usage record per model request (`providerData.usage.requests == 1`, unique `providerData.messageId`), so every session reported roughly one request's tokens and cost.

Measured on 117 local WorkBuddy sessions (3,928 usage records):

| | Total tokens |
|---|---|
| Before (last record only) | ~10.8M |
| After / hand-summed per request | 434.4M |

One 319-request session: 89.8K tokens / $0.07 before → 85.8M tokens / $12.26 after.

## Fix
- Emit a timestamped `meta` event for every usage record, deduplicated by `providerData.messageId` (same pattern as the Claude Code parser). This also feeds per-request timestamps into `--daily` / `--blocks`.
- Document the `input_tokens` basis on `workbuddy_usage`: it **includes** cached input (`total_tokens == input_tokens + output_tokens` on 3909/3909 records that carry `total_tokens`), so subtracting `cache_read_input_tokens` is correct. The `max(0)` clamp never fired on real data.
- Bump `SESSION_CACHE_SCHEMA_VERSION` 24 → 25 so cached WorkBuddy sessions are reparsed.

## Tests
- The WorkBuddy contract test now asserts that both usage records are summed, that a repeated `messageId` counts once, and that two usage points are recorded.
- Compared all 117 local sessions against a hand count: 112 match exactly. The other 5 have no usage records and keep the existing text-based estimate.

`cargo test --workspace`, `cargo clippy --all-targets -D warnings`, `cargo fmt --check`, and `check-i18n.sh` all pass.

title: fix(install): detect architecture when PSReadLine shadows RuntimeInformation
body:
## Problem

Running the documented Windows one-liner in an interactive Windows PowerShell 5.1 session fails on a normal x64 machine:

```
PS> irm https://raw.githubusercontent.com/luoyuctl/agenttrace/master/install.ps1 | iex
Unsupported architecture:
```

Interactive 5.1 sessions load the bundled **PSReadLine 2.0.0**, which ships its own `System.Runtime.InteropServices.RuntimeInformation` type. That copy wins type resolution (`[RuntimeInformation].Assembly.Location` points to `Microsoft.PowerShell.PSReadLine.dll`), and its `OSArchitecture` is empty. The `switch` then falls through to `default`. Non-interactive runs (`powershell -File`, `install.cmd`, CI) don't load PSReadLine, so they work, which is why CI didn't catch this.

## Fix

- Read `OSArchitecture` as a string, and fall back to `PROCESSOR_ARCHITEW6432` / `PROCESSOR_ARCHITECTURE` when it is empty or throws. `PROCESSOR_ARCHITEW6432` covers a 32-bit shell on a 64-bit OS.
- Accept both `X64` and `AMD64` (env var spelling). `Arm64` already matches `ARM64` because `switch` is case-insensitive.
- Quote the detected value in the error so an empty value is visible.

## Verification (Windows 11 x64, PowerShell 5.1.26100)

| Scenario | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| Interactive PS 5.1 with PSReadLine 2.0.0 (`OSArchitecture` = empty) | ❌ `Unsupported architecture:` | ✅ downloaded windows/amd64, SHA-256 verified, `agenttrace --version` → v0.10.1 |
| `powershell -NoProfile -File install.ps1` | ✅ | ✅ |

- PowerShell parser: 0 errors
- `scripts/ci/check-release-surfaces.sh`: passes

title: fix(install): drop the CMD installer and make version pinning work on Windows
body:
## Summary

Two Windows installer cleanups:

1. Remove `install.cmd` and the "Windows CMD" install route. `install.ps1` (`irm … | iex`) is now the only Windows installer.
2. Make version pinning actually work on Windows. `install.ps1` now honors `AGENTTRACE_VERSION`, and the README shows a pin command that works on each platform.

## 1. Drop the CMD installer

- `install.cmd` only downloaded `install.ps1` and ran it with `powershell -File`. That avoided the PSReadLine `RuntimeInformation` shadowing bug, but #314 fixed that bug in `install.ps1` itself.
- The CMD one-liner was more fragile than the PowerShell one:
  - It wrote `install.cmd` into the current directory. That overwrote any file with the same name, failed where the directory isn't writable (an elevated CMD starts in `System32`), and left the file behind when the install failed, because `&& del` was skipped.
  - Pasted into Windows PowerShell 5.1, it failed outright: `curl` there is an alias for `Invoke-WebRequest`, which rejects `-fsSL`.

## 2. Version pinning on Windows

The README said to pin with `AGENTTRACE_VERSION=v0.9.1` "(or `-Version v0.9.1` in PowerShell)". Neither worked for the documented Windows install:
- `install.ps1` never read `AGENTTRACE_VERSION`.
- Parameters such as `-Version` can't reach a script run through `irm | iex`.

`install.ps1` now uses the same environment variables as `install.sh` as its parameter defaults: `AGENTTRACE_VERSION`, `AGENTTRACE_INSTALL_DIR`, and `AGENTTRACE_NO_MODIFY_PATH=1`. Explicit parameters still win when the script is run with `-File`.

The README now shows a working pin command for each platform:

```powershell
$env:AGENTTRACE_VERSION = "v0.9.1"; irm https://raw.githubusercontent.com/luoyuctl/agenttrace/master/install.ps1 | iex
```

## Changes

- Delete `install.cmd`
- `install.ps1`: read `AGENTTRACE_VERSION` / `AGENTTRACE_INSTALL_DIR` / `AGENTTRACE_NO_MODIFY_PATH` as parameter defaults, and document them in the header
- `README.md`, `README.zh-CN.md`: remove the "Windows CMD" section and replace the pinning sentence with per-platform commands
- `docs/maintainers/distribution.md`: drop the `install.cmd` references
- `scripts/ci/check-release-surfaces.sh`: drop the check that `install.cmd` delegates to `install.ps1`

## Verification (Windows 11 x64, interactive PowerShell 5.1)

| Scenario | Result |
|---|---|
| `irm \| iex` style with `AGENTTRACE_VERSION=v0.10.0`, `AGENTTRACE_INSTALL_DIR`, `AGENTTRACE_NO_MODIFY_PATH=1` | ✅ installed v0.10.0 into the given dir, SHA-256 verified, user PATH unchanged |
| `-File install.ps1 -Version v0.10.1` with `AGENTTRACE_VERSION=v0.10.0` still set | ✅ explicit parameter wins → v0.10.1 |

- PowerShell parser: 0 errors
- `scripts/ci/check-release-surfaces.sh` passes
- No remaining references to `install.cmd` in the repo

## Note

The old raw URL `…/master/install.cmd` will return 404 after this merges. Anyone who copied the CMD one-liner from an older README will get a download error and should use the PowerShell command instead.

title: fix(parser): clamp cache counts to cache-inclusive input
body:
## Summary

WorkBuddy and Copilot report `input_tokens` inclusive of cached input, and the parser subtracts the cache counts to get uncached input. When a ledger's cache count exceeded its input, uncached input was floored at 0 but the cache count was kept, so the session total grew past what the source recorded (e.g. `input 100, cache_read 150` → input 0 + cache read 150 = 150 > 100).

`subtract_cached_input` now clamps each cache count to what is left of the input, matching ccusage (`cached.min(input)` + `saturating_sub`) and CodexBar. WorkBuddy uses the same helper instead of its own inline subtraction. Codex is unchanged: its contract test intentionally keeps the delta cache read unclamped (`rust_codex_rollout_clamps_negative_uncached_input_like_go`).

Session cache schema bumped to 27 so cached sessions are re-parsed.

## Coordination

- Linked issue: #310 (residual `.max(0)` nit)

- Parser PR mergeability checked after latest `master`? yes

- [x] `cargo fmt --check`

New contract test `rust_workbuddy_clamps_cache_read_above_input_without_inflating_total`. On 3928 local WorkBuddy usage records, none have `cache_read > input_tokens`, so real totals are unchanged.

body:
## Summary

Supersedes #309. Dependabot's grouped bump failed to compile because ureq 3 changed its API. This PR takes the same 8 updates, one commit per risk level:

| Commit | Change | Code changes |
|---|---|---|
| patch bumps | clap 4.6.3, serde 1.0.229, serde_json 1.0.151, thiserror 2.0.21 | none |

| rusqlite 0.40 | — | none |

ureq 3 migration:
- `AgentBuilder` → `Agent::config_builder()`. `timeout_read` → `timeout_recv_response`, plus a 10-minute `timeout_recv_body` budget for the release binary. `redirects(0)` → `max_redirects(0)`.
- `.set()` → `.header()`; `response.header()` → `headers().get()`.
- `into_string()` → `body_mut().read_to_string()`; `into_reader()` → `into_body().into_reader()`.
- The pricing download raises ureq 3's default 10 MB string-body limit to 64 MB. The LiteLLM table is ~3 MB and growing.

Updates `github/codeql-action/upload-sarif` from 4.38.2 to 4.39.0
Release notes

Sourced from github/codeql-action/upload-sarif's releases.

v4.39.0

  • Breaking change: Bump the minimum required CodeQL bundle version to 2.20.7. #4205
  • The codeql-action/analyze step now validates that a correct argument for the checkout_path input has been provided. The checkout_path input must be set to the path where the repository that is being analyzed is checked out at on the runner, if that path is something other than the workspace root. If the path does not point to a repository checkout or is different from the path that was used by codeql-action/init, then the CodeQL Action now produces a warning. #4148
  • Resolved an issue with third-party caching implementations that prevented caches from being restored correctly. #4206
  • The codeql-action/start-proxy step that is used in Code Scanning Default Setup now finds CodeQL releases using the same logic as codeql-action/init. This primarily benefits customers who are using GitHub instances other than github.com where the codeql-action/start-proxy step may previously have been unable to locate recent releases and ended up using outdated versions of the private registry authentication proxy as a result. #4198

v4.38.3

  • Upcoming breaking change: CodeQL version 2.21.2 and earlier were discontinued on 24 September 2026 alongside GitHub Enterprise Server 3.17, and will be unsupported by the next minor release of the CodeQL Action. Added a deprecation warning for customers using these versions of CodeQL. #4188
  • Update default CodeQL bundle version to 2.27.2. #4203
  • Fixed a bug where the decision of whether to use a per-language bundle did not account for custom configurations that reference queries outside of compiled CodeQL packs. This issue was caught during internal testing and did not affect any customer repositories. We will resume the roll out of per-language bundles in the coming weeks. #4184
Changelog

CodeQL Action Changelog

See the releases page for the relevant changes to the CodeQL CLI and language packs.

[UNRELEASED]

4.39.0 - 15 Oct 2026

  • Breaking change: Bump the minimum required CodeQL bundle version to 2.20.7. #4205
  • The codeql-action/analyze step now validates that a correct argument for the checkout_path input has been provided. The checkout_path input must be set to the path where the repository that is being analyzed is checked out at on the runner, if that path is something other than the workspace root. If the path does not point to a repository checkout or is different from the path that was used by codeql-action/init, then the CodeQL Action now produces a warning. #4148
  • Resolved an issue with third-party caching implementations that prevented caches from being restored correctly. #4206
  • The codeql-action/start-proxy step that is used in Code Scanning Default Setup now finds CodeQL releases using the same logic as codeql-action/init. This primarily benefits customers who are using GitHub instances other than github.com where the codeql-action/start-proxy step may previously have been unable to locate recent releases and ended up using outdated versions of the private registry authentication proxy as a result. #4198

4.38.3 - 08 Oct 2026

  • Upcoming breaking change: CodeQL version 2.21.2 and earlier were discontinued on 24 September 2026 alongside GitHub Enterprise Server 3.17, and will be unsupported by the next minor release of the CodeQL Action. Added a deprecation warning for customers using these versions of CodeQL. #4188
  • Update default CodeQL bundle version to 2.27.2. #4203
  • Fixed a bug where the decision of whether to use a per-language bundle did not account for custom configurations that reference queries outside of compiled CodeQL packs. This issue was caught during internal testing and did not affect any customer repositories. We will resume the roll out of per-language bundles in the coming weeks. #4184

  • The codeql-action/analyze step now validates that a correct argument for the checkout_path input has been provided.   • Update default CodeQL bundle version to 2.27.2. #4203
  • Fixed a bug where the decision of whether to use a per-language bundle did not account for custom configurations that reference queries outside of compiled CodeQL packs. The checkout_path input must be set to the path where the repository that is being analyzed is checked out at on the runner, if that path is something other than the workspace root. If the path does not point to a repository checkout or is different from the path that was used by codeql-action/init, then the CodeQL Action now produces a warning. #4148
  • Resolved an issue with third-party caching implementations that prevented caches from being restored correctly. #4206
  • The codeql-action/start-proxy step that is used in Code Scanning Default Setup now finds CodeQL releases using the same logic as codeql-action/init. This primarily benefits customers who are using GitHub instances other than github.com where the codeql-action/start-proxy step may previously have been unable to locate recent releases and ended up using outdated versions of the private registry authentication proxy as a result. #4198

  • Update default CodeQL bundle version to 2.27.2. #4203

Updates `github/codeql-action/upload-sarif` from 4.38.2 to 4.39.3
Release notes

Sourced from github/codeql-action/upload-sarif's releases.

v4.39.3

  • Fixed diff-informed alert filtering incorrectly removing alerts in changed files whose paths contain spaces, special characters, or non-ASCII characters. #4283

v4.39.2

  • Update default CodeQL bundle version to 2.27.4. #4284
  • Upcoming breaking change: CodeQL version 2.22.3 and earlier were discontinued on 16 October 2026 alongside GitHub Enterprise Server 3.18, and will be unsupported by the next minor release of the CodeQL Action. Added a deprecation warning for customers using these versions of CodeQL. #4266
  • Starting with macOS 27 and Xcode 27, traced analyses are unsupported. See this blog post for more information. The CodeQL Action will now try to identify if a workflow is about to perform a traced analysis on version 27 or above of macOS or Xcode. If so, the CodeQL Action will emit a corresponding warning that will also be visible on the Tool Status Page. This check will be rolled out following this release of the CodeQL Action. #4221
  • The undocumented TRAP cache cleanup feature that could be enabled using the CODEQL_ACTION_CLEANUP_TRAP_CACHES environment variable has been removed, as announced in the release notes for CodeQL Action 4.35.2. The analyze Action now warns if this environment variable is set. If you used TRAP cache cleanup to limit Actions cache usage, we recommend disabling TRAP caching by passing the trap-caching: false input to the init Action. #4243

v4.39.1

  • Update default CodeQL bundle version to 2.27.3. #4256

v4.39.0

  • Breaking change: Bump the minimum required CodeQL bundle version to 2.20.7. #4205
